children.text: An ideal gas fills a sealed insulating tube of length \(L\) and cross-section \(S\), along x. Equilibrium pressure, temperature and density are \(p_0,T_0,\rho_0\). Ignore viscosity and transverse variation. A small standing-wave displacement is \(u(x,t)=a\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t)\), with \(a\ll L\) and \(k=2\pi/\lambda\). Use the longest allowed wavelength throughout. A narrow parcel has \(V_0=S\Delta x\). Write \(V=V_0+V_1(x)\cos\omega t\), \(p=p_0-p_1(x)\cos\omega t\), and \(T=T_0-T_1(x)\cos\omega t\). Changes are small, and compression is adiabatic with index \(\gamma\) unless thermal contact is specified.
Use forces on a parcel to find the pressure coefficient.
Find sound speed using the adiabatic relation.
A.6. Thermal effect on the tube
For this task only, allow weak thermal interaction with the tube while keeping the wave approximately unchanged. State long-time temperature changes at the left end A, centre B and right end C.

nodes.alt: Original tube with short parallel-plate stack at L/4, hot and cold reservoir connections and stack edges.

children.text: A short stack of plates parallel to x is centred at \(x_0=L/4\), length \(\ell\ll L\), filling cross-section \(S\). Its left and right edges are held at \(T_H=T_0+\tau/2\) and \(T_C=T_0-\tau/2\). The plate temperature is \(T_0-(x-x_0)\tau/\ell\). For a parcel at \(x_0\), write its local environment temperature as \(T_0-T_{st}\cos\omega t\) and find \(T_{st}\).

Find the critical \(\tau_{cr}\) above which gas transports heat from hot to cold. Assume \(\tau\ll T_0\), nearly uniform pressure and displacement over the stack, no edge effects, and negligible axial conduction. Only gas-stack conduction and convective transport matter.
Find \(dQ/dt\) in terms of \(\dot V,\dot p,p_0,V_0,\gamma\). You may use \(c_v=R/(\gamma-1)\).

The heat input is \(\dot Q=-\beta V_0(T_{st}-T_1)\cos\omega t\), with \(\beta>0\). Its temperature perturbation is negligible at operating frequency. Write \(p=p_0+p_a\sin\omega t-p_b\cos\omega t\), \(V=V_0+V_a\sin\omega t+V_b\cos\omega t\). Given \(p_a,p_b\), find \(V_a,V_b\).
Find work per parcel volume over a cycle, then total work \(W_{tot}\) over the stack.
Find heat carried from left to right across \(x=x_0\) per cycle. You may use convective current \(j=Q\,du/dt\).
Find the ratio of acoustic work to heat drawn from the hot reservoir, in terms of \(\tau,\tau_{cr}\) and Carnot efficiency \(\eta_c=1-T_C/T_H\).

statement.text:
Thermoacoustic Engine
An ideal gas fills a sealed insulating tube of length \(L\) and cross-section \(S\), along x. Equilibrium pressure, temperature and density are \(p_0,T_0,\rho_0\). Ignore viscosity and transverse variation. A small standing-wave displacement is \(u(x,t)=a\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t)\), with \(a\ll L\) and \(k=2\pi/\lambda\). Use the longest allowed wavelength throughout. A narrow parcel has \(V_0=S\Delta x\). Write \(V=V_0+V_1(x)\cos\omega t\), \(p=p_0-p_1(x)\cos\omega t\), and \(T=T_0-T_1(x)\cos\omega t\). Changes are small, and compression is adiabatic with index \(\gamma\) unless thermal contact is specified.
A.1. Longest wavelength
Find the longest allowed wavelength.
A.2. Volume amplitude
Find the signed volume-oscillation coefficient.
A.3. Pressure amplitude
Use forces on a parcel to find the pressure coefficient.
A.4. Sound speed
Find sound speed using the adiabatic relation.
A.5. Temperature amplitude
Find the temperature coefficient.
A.6. Thermal effect on the tube
For this task only, allow weak thermal interaction with the tube while keeping the wave approximately unchanged. State long-time temperature changes at the left end A, centre B and right end C.
B.1. Stack temperature amplitude

A short stack of plates parallel to x is centred at \(x_0=L/4\), length \(\ell\ll L\), filling cross-section \(S\). Its left and right edges are held at \(T_H=T_0+\tau/2\) and \(T_C=T_0-\tau/2\). The plate temperature is \(T_0-(x-x_0)\tau/\ell\). For a parcel at \(x_0\), write its local environment temperature as \(T_0-T_{st}\cos\omega t\) and find \(T_{st}\).
B.2. Critical thermal gradient
Find the critical \(\tau_{cr}\) above which gas transports heat from hot to cold. Assume \(\tau\ll T_0\), nearly uniform pressure and displacement over the stack, no edge effects, and negligible axial conduction. Only gas-stack conduction and convective transport matter.
B.3. Linearized heat-flow law
Find \(dQ/dt\) in terms of \(\dot V,\dot p,p_0,V_0,\gamma\). You may use \(c_v=R/(\gamma-1)\).
B.4. Volume phase coefficients
The heat input is \(\dot Q=-\beta V_0(T_{st}-T_1)\cos\omega t\), with \(\beta>0\). Its temperature perturbation is negligible at operating frequency. Write \(p=p_0+p_a\sin\omega t-p_b\cos\omega t\), \(V=V_0+V_a\sin\omega t+V_b\cos\omega t\). Given \(p_a,p_b\), find \(V_a,V_b\).
B.5. Acoustic work
Find work per parcel volume over a cycle, then total work \(W_{tot}\) over the stack.
B.6. Heat transported per cycle
Find heat carried from left to right across \(x=x_0\) per cycle. You may use convective current \(j=Q\,du/dt\).
B.7. Engine efficiency
Find the ratio of acoustic work to heat drawn from the hot reservoir, in terms of \(\tau,\tau_{cr}\) and Carnot efficiency \(\eta_c=1-T_C/T_H\).

children.text: Displacement vanishes at both sealed ends, so the fundamental has \(kL=\pi\) and \(\lambda_{max}=2L\).
The length change is \(\Delta x\,\partial u/\partial x\). Thus \(V_1=akV_0\cos kx\).
Linearized Newton's law is \(\rho_0\ddot u=-\partial p/\partial x\). Integrate in x to obtain \[p_1=\frac{a\omega^2\rho_0}{k}\cos kx.\]
Linearize the ideal-gas relation: \(T_1/T_0=p_1/p_0-V_1/V_0\). Thus \(T_1=ak(\gamma-1)T_0\cos kx\).
A.6. Thermal effect on the tube

Displacement and temperature are correlated so parcels carry heat away from the centre towards both ends. A and C warm, while B cools. The effect is thermal pumping by the acoustic motion, not viscous heating.
Heat follows hot to cold when \(T_{st}>T_1(x_0)\). Equating amplitudes gives \[\tau_{cr}=k\ell(\gamma-1)T_0.\]
From \(E=pV/(\gamma-1)\) and \(\dot Q=\dot E+p\dot V\), keep first-order changes: \[\dot Q=\frac{V_0\dot p+\gamma p_0\dot V}{\gamma-1}.\]

Match cosine and sine in B3, using \(T_{st}-T_1=a(\tau-\tau_{cr})/(\ell\sqrt2)\): \[V_b=\frac{V_0p_b}{\gamma p_0},\quad V_a=-\frac{V_0}{\gamma p_0}\left[p_a+\frac{(\gamma-1)\beta a(\tau-\tau_{cr})}{\omega\ell\sqrt2}\right].\] The source has an intermediate sign typo in its heat-input substitution. These final coefficients follow the question's negative heat-input convention.
Integrate \(\oint p\,dV=-\pi(p_aV_b+p_bV_a)\). Thus \(w=-\pi(p_aV_b+p_bV_a)/V_0\). With leading \(p_b=ak\gamma p_0/\sqrt2\), \[W_{tot}=wS\ell=\frac\pi{2\omega}(\gamma-1)\beta(\tau-\tau_{cr})ka^2S.\]

Integration by parts of the convected heat gives \(Q_{tot}=-(1/\Delta x)\oint\dot Q\,u\,dt\). Substitute the heat-input and displacement cosines: \[Q_{tot}=\frac\pi{2\omega}\frac{\beta(\tau-\tau_{cr})a^2S}{\ell}.\]

Dividing B5 by B6 gives \(\eta=(\gamma-1)k\ell=\tau_{cr}/T_0\). Since \(\eta_c\simeq\tau/T_0\) for \(\tau\ll T_0\), \[\eta\simeq\frac{\tau_{cr}}\tau\eta_c.\] This is the leading weak-gradient result on the engine branch \(\tau>\tau_{cr}\).

solution.text:
Thermoacoustic Engine
A.1. Longest wavelength
Displacement vanishes at both sealed ends, so the fundamental has \(kL=\pi\) and \(\lambda_{max}=2L\).
A.2. Volume amplitude
The length change is \(\Delta x\,\partial u/\partial x\). Thus \(V_1=akV_0\cos kx\).
A.3. Pressure amplitude
Linearized Newton's law is \(\rho_0\ddot u=-\partial p/\partial x\). Integrate in x to obtain \[p_1=\frac{a\omega^2\rho_0}{k}\cos kx.\]
A.4. Sound speed
Linearizing \(pV^\gamma=\mathrm{constant}\) gives \(p_1/p_0=\gamma V_1/V_0\). Therefore \(c=\omega/k=\sqrt{\gamma p_0/\rho_0}\).
A.5. Temperature amplitude
Linearize the ideal-gas relation: \(T_1/T_0=p_1/p_0-V_1/V_0\). Thus \(T_1=ak(\gamma-1)T_0\cos kx\).
A.6. Thermal effect on the tube
Displacement and temperature are correlated so parcels carry heat away from the centre towards both ends. A and C warm, while B cools. The effect is thermal pumping by the acoustic motion, not viscous heating.
B.1. Stack temperature amplitude
Substitute parcel displacement \(u(x_0,t)=a\cos\omega t/\sqrt2\). Then \(T_{st}=a\tau/(\ell\sqrt2)\).
B.2. Critical thermal gradient
Heat follows hot to cold when \(T_{st}>T_1(x_0)\). Equating amplitudes gives \[\tau_{cr}=k\ell(\gamma-1)T_0.\]
B.3. Linearized heat-flow law
From \(E=pV/(\gamma-1)\) and \(\dot Q=\dot E+p\dot V\), keep first-order changes: \[\dot Q=\frac{V_0\dot p+\gamma p_0\dot V}{\gamma-1}.\]
B.4. Volume phase coefficients
Match cosine and sine in B3, using \(T_{st}-T_1=a(\tau-\tau_{cr})/(\ell\sqrt2)\): \[V_b=\frac{V_0p_b}{\gamma p_0},\quad V_a=-\frac{V_0}{\gamma p_0}\left[p_a+\frac{(\gamma-1)\beta a(\tau-\tau_{cr})}{\omega\ell\sqrt2}\right].\] The source has an intermediate sign typo in its heat-input substitution. These final coefficients follow the question's negative heat-input convention.
B.5. Acoustic work
Integrate \(\oint p\,dV=-\pi(p_aV_b+p_bV_a)\). Thus \(w=-\pi(p_aV_b+p_bV_a)/V_0\). With leading \(p_b=ak\gamma p_0/\sqrt2\), \[W_{tot}=wS\ell=\frac\pi{2\omega}(\gamma-1)\beta(\tau-\tau_{cr})ka^2S.\]
B.6. Heat transported per cycle
Integration by parts of the convected heat gives \(Q_{tot}=-(1/\Delta x)\oint\dot Q\,u\,dt\). Substitute the heat-input and displacement cosines: \[Q_{tot}=\frac\pi{2\omega}\frac{\beta(\tau-\tau_{cr})a^2S}{\ell}.\]
B.7. Engine efficiency
Dividing B5 by B6 gives \(\eta=(\gamma-1)k\ell=\tau_{cr}/T_0\). Since \(\eta_c\simeq\tau/T_0\) for \(\tau\ll T_0\), \[\eta\simeq\frac{\tau_{cr}}\tau\eta_c.\] This is the leading weak-gradient result on the engine branch \(\tau>\tau_{cr}\).
